summary: Added early-return guard to propagateDependencyUnblock in work-package.ts. Before entering the batch lock, the function now calls store.readRootIndex() and checks whether any BLOCKED WP in the root index has completedWpId in its dependencies list. If none are found, the function returns immediately — skipping lock acquisition, the second root index read inside the batch, all WP detail reads, and the root index + meta sync write. The batch method still re-reads inside its lock on the non-early-return path, making the optimization safe under concurrent writes.

comments.note: propagateDependencyReblock (line ~1028) has the same structure as propagateDependencyUnblock and could benefit from an identical early-return guard. It also unconditionally enters batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync even when no READY/IN_PROGRESS dependents exist. This is out of scope for WP-001 but worth a follow-up.

The pre-check read in propagateDependencyUnblock introduces a small redundancy: rootIndex is read twice on the hot path (once for the pre-check, once inside the batch lock). A comment already explains why this is safe and intentional, but a future refactor could plumb the pre-check result into the batch callback to avoid the second read — this would require a batch API change and is not worth doing here.

summary: Full verification stack passed. Early-return guard in propagateDependencyUnblock is correct: reads root index outside the lock, checks for any BLOCKED WP with completedWpId in its dependencies, returns immediately if none found. The guard skips lock acquisition, the in-batch root index read, all WP detail reads, and the meta sync write — all of which are appropriate to skip when there are no candidates. No side effects are incorrectly skipped. The batch path is entirely unchanged on the hot path (when candidates do exist). All 44 test files and 1432 tests pass.

comments.note: No explicit test exists for the early-return path itself (i.e., a scenario where propagateDependencyUnblock is called with completedWpId that has zero BLOCKED dependents, verifying batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync is not called). The guard logic is trivially correct and indirectly covered, but a direct unit test would increase confidence for future refactors.

rootIndex.last_updated is unconditionally set inside the batch callback even when updatedWps is empty. The early-return guard now bypasses this unnecessary timestamp update in the no-candidates case — this is a correct and beneficial side effect of the guard.
No observations on code quality or correctness issues — code is clean, well-commented, and consistent with surrounding patterns in the file.

summary: Code review PASS. The early-return guard in propagateDependencyUnblock (lines 966-986) is correct, well-scoped, and follows the standard optimistic-skip / authoritative-re-check pattern. Race condition is acceptably bounded. Guard filter is an exact match to the batch callback filter. No necessary side effects are skipped. Comments are accurate and sufficient.

comments.note: The pre-check filter (status === 'BLOCKED' && dependencies.includes(completedWpId)) exactly mirrors the batch callback filter. The guard correctly operates at 'are there candidates worth acquiring the lock for?' granularity rather than predicting the final transition set — this is the right abstraction boundary.

Race condition is acceptably bounded. False positive (WP transitions away from BLOCKED before lock): batch callback re-filters and updatedWps is empty, incurring only lock overhead. False negative (WP becomes BLOCKED after pre-check): missed on this call, caught on next dependency completion. Comment at lines 973-977 accurately documents this. Minor nit: comment says 'next status transition' but the miss is caught on the next *completion* of another dependency — not a blocking issue.

The rootIndex.last_updated unconditional write inside the batch callback (line 1021) is correctly bypassed by the guard when there are no candidates. QA noted this as a beneficial side effect; confirmed correct from review perspective.
No blocking issues. Code is clean, consistent with surrounding patterns, and the double root-index read on the hot path is documented and justified. No changes required.
